notes: SHIP v1.14.459 - TEST PAYLOAD FOR THE .458 UPDATE-PATH FIX. THIS SHIP DELIBERATELY CHANGES NO BEHAVIOUR. It is three version stamps and nothing else - no logic, no markup, no styling, no assets. That is the entire point: .458 rebuilt the service-worker update path after the SW UPDATE button failed to complete an update on a real installed iPhone PWA, and the only honest way to verify that fix is to publish a build whose sole observable difference is the version number. If the visible stamp moves from .458 to .459 after one tap, the mechanism works; nothing else in the app can account for the change. WHAT IS BEING TESTED, in order: a new worker installs and parks in WAITING rather than skipping straight past it; the SW UPDATE badge appears only because phantom_swActionable found that waiting worker; one tap calls phantom_swApplyUpdate, the single activation door; it posts SKIP_WAITING and the message handler added in .458 promotes the worker; activation fires controllerchange; the one guarded listener performs exactly ONE reload; the navigation fetches with cache reload so the HTTP cache cannot serve the old shell; and the new stamp is visible. SEQUENCING MATTERS AND IS EASY TO GET WRONG. The device must already be RUNNING .458 before this is tapped, because .458 contains the fixed mechanism. A device sitting on .457 is still on the broken path and will jump straight here without exercising anything - in which case this ship proves nothing and a further no-op payload is needed to run the real test. WHAT MUST SURVIVE: the site profile, the active Master, rack and work records, event log and evidence. Application shell cache is not operational truth, and an update that clears field data to get itself unstuck has destroyed the thing the app exists to hold. GATES: three-stamp lockstep at .459, inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, brace balance, 0 bare LF, 0 mojibake. No spec run is claimed for this ship because no code changed; .458's suite is the coverage.
